disease_label_per_paper: Isolated splenic abscess in brucellosis caused by Brucella melitensis
presentation_summary: 50-year-old male milk vendor from rural Bangalore presented with 2 months of fever of unknown origin and acute admission for abdominal pain, high-grade fever with chills, malaise, night sweats, and more than 10 kg weight loss over 45 days.
Exposure history included routine consumption of unpasteurized/raw milk.

Admission exam showed temperature 40 degC, blood pressure 86/60 mmHg, heart rate 120/min, respiratory rate 30/min, severe dehydration, pallor, and left hypochondriac tenderness with a positive Castell sign.
Initial labs showed WBC 32.1 x10^9/L, ESR 100 mm/h, CRP 92 mg/L, hemoglobin 10 g/dL, platelets 199 x10^9/L, creatinine 2.0 mg/dL, blood urea 70 mg/dL, and bicarbonate 17.9 mmol/L.

Ultrasound and CT showed splenomegaly and a 3.2 x 2.8 x 2.8 cm hypodense nonenhancing upper-pole splenic lesion with perisplenic fat stranding; chest radiograph showed bilateral pleural effusion with basal atelectasis.

Echocardiography was normal ... no features of endocarditis were found

confirmatory_findings.finding: Brucella slide and tube agglutination tests positive
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Brucella slide and tube agglutination tests (Wright, at 1/640) were positive
Blood cultures confirmed infection by Brucella melitensis on Day 1 and Day 3

outcome.clinical_course: Improved over 10 days, discharged on day 10, asymptomatic without recurrence at 6 months.
outcome.source_text_value: remained asymptomatic without recurrence at 6 months after completion of treatment

quality_warnings: Brucella culture/speciation and agglutination are kept in confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
Ordinary observations retain presentation-time fever, exposure, shock/dehydration physiology, inflammatory labs, renal dysfunction, and imaging-defined splenic abscess.
